title: Heat pump thermodynamics
summary: How the Carnot limit and the temperature lift set a heat pump's efficiency, and how the house's emitters set the lift.

concepts.label: Heat pump
concepts.description: An air-to-water vapour-compression heat pump: evaporator outside, condenser in the heating water.

facts.text: HeatpumpMonitor.org publishes metered data of several hundred domestic heat pumps.

children.label: Coefficient of performance
children.description: Heat out / electricity in, per day (COP) or per year (SCOP).

children.label: Share of Carnot
children.description: Measured COP / Carnot COP: how close the machine gets to the ideal.

children.label: Defrost and cycling
children.description: Losses on cold, humid days (ice on the evaporator) and at low load (on/off cycling).

concepts.label: Carnot limit
concepts.description: COP_max = T_hot/(T_hot − T_cold) in kelvin, from the second law of thermodynamics.

facts.text: A reversed Carnot cycle is the most efficient possible heat pump between two temperatures.

children.label: Temperature lift
children.description: Flow temperature minus outdoor temperature, K.

children.label: Refrigerant temperatures
children.description: Condensing and evaporating temperatures, a few kelvin beyond the water and the air; not in the data.

concepts.label: Heating system
concepts.description: The emitters and controls that set the flow temperature.

children.label: Underfloor heating
children.description: Large emitting area: low flow temperature.

children.label: Radiators
children.description: Smaller area: higher flow temperature, unless oversized.

children.label: Weather compensation
children.description: Flow temperature set from the outdoor temperature, as low as the day allows.

concepts.label: Weather
concepts.description: Daily mean outdoor temperature at the unit, °C.

concepts.label: Building heat loss
concepts.description: kW per kelvin of indoor–outdoor difference; sets the heat demand and the emitter size needed.
